rfi.title: Survivors of Guinea's deadly landfill collapse say authorities ignored warnings
rfi.description: Two days after a deadly landfill collapse in Guinea, rescuers are using giant excavators to search for victims. Anger is rising among residents, who say they had warned authorities that the rubbish dump was precarious.

rfi.title: At least 40 killed as gangs attack displaced people near Haiti capital
rfi.description: At least 40 people have been killed, some execution-style, after gangs attacked displaced people sheltering in a church near Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince at the weekend, local authorities said.

rfi.title: French village reels from tornado that damaged hundreds of homes
rfi.description: Hundreds of damaged homes, widespread power cuts and blocked roads confronted residents of southwestern France on Tuesday after a tornado tore through the village of Pomas, injuring 39 people, two of them critically.

rfi.title: French astronaut Adenot undertakes second spacewalk to finish ISS repairs
rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot on Tuesday stepped outside the International Space Station (ISS) for the second time, a week after she became the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Over the coming hours, her mission will be to finish the repairs to an antenna begun on 18 August.

rfi.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
rfi.description: Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry.

rfi.title: Ukraine's allies pledge to continue support with focus on air defence
rfi.description: Ukraine's allies on Monday pledged to keep up their support in the war against Russia, with a renewed focus on air defence investment to counter a shortage of US Patriot interceptors.

rfi.title: Saudi Arabia to invest €6bn in building theme parks near Paris
rfi.description: France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed a memo of understanding for a €6 billion Saudi investment to create three theme parks near Paris, the office of the French president said.

rfi.title: Mediterranean migrant rescue ships threatened by Libyan groups, warns NGO
rfi.description: A leading group monitoring and providing aid to migrants crossing the Mediterranean have warned that its rescue ships have been facing increasing threats and harassment from Libyan groups.

rfi.title: Malian PM's visit to Algeria underlines need for mutual security goals
rfi.description: The acting head of the Malian government, General Abdoulaye Maiga has begun a two-day visit to Algeria. It comes amid a thaw after months of tension. RFI spoke to Bakary Sambe, the Director of the Timbuktu Institute about the security situation and what the countries hope to gain from the meeting.

rfi.title: Six million Somalis face acute hunger as drought and conflict worsen
rfi.description: Six million people in Somalia are facing acute hunger, with nearly two million children at emergency levels, as severe drought, conflict and falling humanitarian funding deepen what the UN describes as one of the world’s worst malnutrition crises. Medical charity MSF tells RFI it's sounding the alarm "before it's too late".

rfi.title: Violence against healthcare workers in DRC hampers Ebola response
rfi.description: Healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been coming under attack, the United Nations and Red Cross have warned, hampering efforts to stem the spread of the Ebola virus, which is spreading 'exponentially'.

rfi.title: Centre-left Glucksmann enters French presidential race as left tries to unite
rfi.description: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann has announced his candidacy for next year's presidential election, seeking to challenge hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon to lead France's fractured left, as a campaign increasingly dominated by the far right takes shape.

rfi.title: Scorching summer takes toll on bees and honey harvests in France
rfi.description: France produces 20,000 tonnes of honey each year, but successive heatwaves and persistent drought across Europe this summer are impacting bee populations as flowering plants dry out and colonies struggle to find food. Beekeeper Romain Lacotte and his family farm 1,000 hives in Haute-Corrèze, central France, an area considered one of the country's natural water towers. But even there, he tells RFI, high temperatures and lack of rain are taking their toll.

rfi.title: DRC and M23 rebels agree on roadmap for peace in eastern Congo
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the M23 rebel group have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks aimed at resolving the protracted conflict in eastern DRC. It marks the latest step in an internationally brokered peace process that has seen the parties make cautious concessions, without ending the fighting.

rfi.title: Saudi crown prince heads to France as Paris seeks closer Gulf ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Sunday for a two-day official visit, as Paris looks to deepen ties with Riyadh against a backdrop of war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Mystery elephant deaths in Kenya leave experts divided over cause
rfi.description: Conservationists and Maasai communities are calling for urgent answers as paralysis-like symptoms spread among elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park, with competing theories emerging over what is causing their deaths.

rfi.title: Togo says it has 'serious' evidence against detained French journalists
rfi.description: Togo's government says it has "serious and consistent evidence" against two French documentary filmmakers detained since July on charges of making false statements. Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani were arrested along with their Togolese fixer, Fred Vedomey, and have denied wrongdoing.

rfi.title: Southern African mothers plead for sons lured to Russia's war in Ukraine
rfi.description: Instead of celebrating her son's birthday this month, Zimbabwean mother Rodwin Chitewere spent the day praying for his body to be brought home from Russia, where he was reportedly killed fighting Moscow's war against Ukraine.

euronews.title: Spain to reform asylum laws to align with EU rules as Ceuta crisis remains unresolved
euronews.description: Spain is set to reform its immigration and asylum laws as the Ceuta crisis remains unresolved. Around 5,000 migrants, including 2,000 minors, remain in the enclave after the mass influx from Morocco in July.

euronews.title: Blacksmiths recreate Viking Age anchor using ancient techniques in Denmark
euronews.description: An international team of blacksmiths is recreating a Viking Age anchor using techniques and materials believed to have been used more than 1,000 years ago.

euronews.title: EXCLUSIVE: France wants to limit Ukraine's non-European procurement with EU money
euronews.description: France seeks time limits on Ukraine's derogations for non-EU defence purchases under €90bn loan, in push for European — and French — producers. Kyiv benefits from exemptions for Chinese and US parts.

euronews.title: Euronews exclusive: EU officials to travel to China as October deadline for trade rebalancing looms
euronews.description: Beijing and Brussels are at loggerheads after China barred its companies from cooperating with the European Commission in antitrust investigations. EU officials will travel to China in the coming days.

euronews.title: Phones, drones and ships running blind as GPS malfunctions across Poland
euronews.description: Poland's National Institute of Telecommunications has said that the source is external and linked to the activity of electronic warfare systems in the Baltic Sea region.

euronews.title: Qatar says officials working daily to revive US-Iran talks, urges Tehran to reopen Hormuz
euronews.description: Qatar says its officials are speaking to the parties daily to restart US-Iran negotiations, while urging Tehran to reopen and immediately restore freedom of navigation through the key energy route.

euronews.description: The rhetoric between the two countries is escalating, with Trump telling Canadian leaders on Monday to “fall in line” or face consequences “far WORSE” than existing tariffs.

euronews.title: Ceuta migration sparks nearly 9,600 hate posts on social media
euronews.description: The Spanish Observatory on Racism and Xenophobia logged 9,590 hate messages in two days tied to a July influx of some 80,000 migrants into Ceuta.

euronews.description: This is not the first time that Oscar-nominated Irish actress Saoirse Ronan has expressed a desire to play a Bond villain... But with her recent comments and her husband currently rumoured to be the frontrunner for the next 007, we need this casting to happen now more than ever.

euronews.title: One million Afghan children suffering 'life-threatening' malnutrition, UNICEF says
euronews.description: Afghanistan has endured repeated periods of widespread hunger in recent decades as it has struggled through civil war and other crises.

euronews.title: Mobilisation fears grip Russians as Kremlin's forced recruitment spikes
euronews.description: Human rights groups said they recorded a surge in forced recruitment since mid-August, amid reports that Russia is preparing a new mobilisation wave after September's elections.

euronews.title: Finnair cancels Dubai flights for entire winter season
euronews.description: The Finnish carrier says continuing instability in the Middle East means services will remain suspended until March 2027.

euronews.title: Why do some people live past 100? Study finds clues in the cells of centenarians
euronews.description: Researchers have identified a rare immune cell that becomes far more common among people who live past 100, pointing to new clues about healthy ageing.

euronews.title: European conservatives and liberals join forces to urge EU to freeze €770 million in Romania funds over mayor
euronews.description: Romania risks losing up to €770 million as a deadline looms for completing reforms, including a disputed law that could oust liberal leader and mayor Dominic Fritz. European conservatives and liberals are calling for the funds to be blocked.

euronews.title: Del Vecchio quits EssilorLuxottica, says bosses 'too distant' from workers
euronews.description: The 31-year-old quits as Ray-Ban president and chief strategy officer, attacking the group's "remote" management, recalling his father's "close to people" style and confirming his role as shareholder through Delfin.

euronews.title: Australia bans AI-generated music from its official charts
euronews.description: Australia's move comes as AI music floods streaming platforms, with a new study finding 38.5% of music released globally in July involved AI.

euronews.title: Swedish military seeks to seize property near naval base owned by Russian with Kremlin ties
euronews.description: Sweden ended two centuries of military non-alignment and joined NATO in 2024 after Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

lemonde.description: Si l’ancien secrétaire général de l’Elysée, Alexis Kohler, s’est exprimé pour défendre le chef de l’Etat, les candidats issus du bloc central critiquent sa pratique du pouvoir tout en essayant de ne pas froisser son électorat.

lemonde.description: Un an après le bombardement de l’hôpital Nasser, qui avait tué vingt-deux personnes dont cinq journalistes dans le sud de la bande de Gaza, un militaire israélien a décrit à plusieurs médias, dont « Le Monde », la façon dont l’armée de l’Etat hébreu cherche par tous les moyens à relier les victimes d’une frappe au Hamas.

lemonde.title: Sophie Adenot a commencé sa deuxième sortie hors de l’ISS, pour terminer sa mission restée inachevée
lemonde.description: Lors de cette mission, qui doit durer environ six heures et demie, l’astronaute française et son coéquipier américain Anil Menon doivent terminer de remplacer une antenne permettant à l’ISS de communiquer avec le centre de contrôle de Houston, au Texas.

lemonde.title: Les Européens doivent accentuer leur soutien à l’Ukraine
lemonde.description: S’ils veulent préserver la paix de leur continent, les valeurs de leurs démocraties et leur prospérité future, les pays européens n’ont pas d’autre choix que de continuer à soutenir l’Ukraine et Volodymyr Zelensky, et même accélérer leur engagement pour ne plus laisser à Vladimir Poutine la latitude de jouer de l’usure du temps qui passe.

lemonde.title: Fernando Cerimedo, l’éminence grise des dirigeants d’extrême droite latino-américains, emprisonné en Bolivie pour tentative de féminicide
lemonde.description: L’Argentin, proche collaborateur du président bolivien, a été arrêté dans l’est du pays après que son ex-compagne, l’avocate Nadia Beller, a été blessée par balles le 17 août. Le parquet soupçonne le stratège en communication et ancien conseiller de Jair Bolsonaro et Javier Milei d’être le commanditaire de l’agression.

lemonde.title: A l’éducation nationale, la valse des réformes vue à travers vingt-cinq ans d’évolution permanente du code de l’éducation
lemonde.description: « Le Monde » a analysé les modifications de ce corpus qui charpente le système scolaire français depuis sa création, en 2000. Le nombre et le rythme des remaniements confirment l’empilement des réformes de l’école, que les enseignants vivent au quotidien et qui figure au rang des motifs de souffrance professionnelle.

lemonde.title: Raphaël Glucksmann promet une « révolution écologique » en cent jours s’il est élu président de la République
lemonde.description: Pour son premier déplacement de campagne, le cofondateur du parti Place publique a choisi le thème de l’éolien. Aux côtés du sénateur Yannick Jadot, il a promis d’engager, dès sa victoire, cent jours de transformation pour « libérer la France » de « son addiction au gaz et au pétrole ».

lemonde.title: Mort de « Dodo la Saumure », proxénète rendu célèbre par l’affaire du Carlton à Lille
lemonde.description: Dominique Alderweireld, tenancier de maisons closes en Belgique, avait été relaxé, ainsi que Dominique Strauss-Kahn, aux côtés duquel il comparaissait, lors du procès pour proxénétisme, en 2015. Il est mort à l’âge de 77 ans à Tournai.

lemonde.title: Tornade dans l’Aude : le village de Pomas partiellement détruit, 39 personnes blessées
lemonde.description: Mardi matin, 1 600 foyers sont toujours privés d’électricité dans le département. Deux personnes sont en urgence absolue, et 300 habitations touchées, selon la préfecture.

lemonde.title: Au Maroc, une grève des avocats longue de plus de cent jours paralyse la justice
lemonde.description: L’Association des barreaux du Maroc proteste depuis le début de l’année contre une nouvelle loi régissant l’exercice du métier d’avocat. Elle voit dans ce texte une « atteinte à leur indépendance ».

lemonde.title: L’artiste chinois Gao Zhen condamné à trois ans de prison pour des sculptures satyriques représentant Mao
lemonde.description: Le plasticien, auteur, au côté de son frère Gao Qiang, d’œuvres iconoclastes dans les années 2000, a été jugé coupable d’avoir diffamé la mémoire du héros national, à l’issue d’un procès à huis clos.

lemonde.title: « Patrick Bruel n’est pas le bienvenu », fait savoir le maire d’Amiens, après les élus de Chartres, Dijon et Strasbourg
lemonde.description: Selon Frédéric Fauvet, le chanteur dispose « d’une liberté que la collectivité n’a pas : celle de renoncer de sa propre initiative » à ses concerts prévus. Une annulation unilatérale constituerait selon lui « une rupture abusive de contrat » et exposerait la collectivité « à un risque juridique et financier majeur »

lemonde.title: « Elle est en train de dormir, et pourtant elle mange » : ces patients qui souffrent d’un trouble alimentaire lié au sommeil
lemonde.description: « Etranges nuits » (7/7). Ce n’est qu’au réveil qu’ils prennent conscience d’avoir ingurgité toutes sortes de produits : gâteaux, conserves froides, voire lessive… Cette « forme hyperspécialisée du somnambulisme » pouvant entraîner une souffrance psychologique reste mal comprise.

lemonde.title: Le zoo de Beauval abandonne son projet d’accueil des dauphins du Marineland d’Antibes
lemonde.description: Le renoncement de Beauval relance l’incertitude sur le sort des dauphins de Marineland, désormais menacés d’un transfert vers l’Asie faute de solution d’accueil en France.

lemonde.title: « Au terme d’un été marqué par les canicules répétées et les incendies ravageurs, la prise de conscience est encore faible et l’impréparation totale »
lemonde.description: Judith Rainhorn, spécialiste de l’histoire environnementale, déplore, dans une tribune au « Monde », l’incapacité des responsables politiques à faire face à l’urgence climatique et appelle à « politiser les désastres ».

Frankreich: Tornado verwüstet Dorf im Südwesten Frankreichs
zeit.description: Ein Tornado hat Häuser in einem Dorf im Südwesten Frankreichs stark beschädigt. Bei dem Unwetter in Pomas wurden 39 Menschen verletzt, zwei davon lebensgefährlich.

zeit.title: Waldbrandgefahr: Brand im Hohen Venn laut EU »offensichtlich« menschlichen Ursprungs
zeit.description: »Vermutlich unabsichtliches, unbewusstes« menschliches Verhalten soll das Feuer im Naturschutzgebiet Hohes Venn verursacht haben. Die EU will daraus Konsequenzen ziehen.

zeit.title: Zuckersteuer: Bundesregierung streitet über Ausgestaltung der Zuckersteuer
zeit.description: Welche Getränke sollen besteuert werden? Und geht es dabei um die Gesundheit – oder um den Bundeshaushalt? Die Regierung ist sich beim Thema Zuckersteuer uneins.

zeit.title: Kabinettsklausur: Opposition fordert grundsätzlichen Kurswechsel der Regierung
zeit.description: Grüne und Linke werfen der Regierung gravierende Versäumnisse beim Klimaschutz vor. Für Kritik sorgt unter anderem die starke Wirtschaftspräsenz bei der Kabinettsklausur.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Ukraine und Partner legen Russland konkrete Friedensvorschläge vor
zeit.description: In einem Thesenpapier schlägt die Ukraine eine Freihandelszone im Donbass vor. Russland weist dies zurück – das besetzte Gebiet sei »russisch«. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Volkswagen-Umbau: VW sieht »etwa die Hälfte« der Stellenstreichungen in Deutschland
zeit.description: Bei VW hat eine Reihe von Betriebsversammlungen begonnen. Konzernchef Oliver Blume äußerte sich zu Sparplänen – und wurde ausgepfiffen.

france24fr.title: Au Kenya, un jeune créateur de mode redonne vie au tissage traditionnel
france24fr.description: 🇰🇪 Au Kenya, un jeune créateur de mode mise sur le tissage manuel pour se démarquer. Il fabrique des tissus et des vêtements à la main, faisant revivre un savoir-faire traditionnel menacé par l’industrialisation.

france24fr.title: Une tornade d'une rare violence balaie un village en France
france24fr.description: Une tornade d’une rare violence a frappé lundi en fin d’après-midi le village de Pomas, près de Carcassonne. En moins de cinq minutes, le phénomène a fait 39 blessés, dont deux personnes en urgence absolue, et a détruit ou endommagé près de 300 habitations. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Sophie Adenot : une deuxième sortie dans l’espace pour achever sa mission
france24fr.description: Une semaine après être devenue la première Française à effectuer une sortie extravéhiculaire, Sophie Adenot retourne à l’extérieur de la Station spatiale internationale, à 400 kilomètres au-dessus de la Terre. Avec l’astronaute américain Anil Menon, elle doit achever le remplacement d’une antenne de communication entre l’ISS et le sol. Reportage de J.Benzina (France 2).

france24fr.title: Tchad : l’armée dénonce une nouvelle incursion liée à la guerre au Soudan
france24fr.description: Selon l’armée tchadienne, des aéronefs et des drones ont poursuivi et bombardé une colonne de véhicules jusque sur le territoire tchadien. Il s’agit de la quatrième incursion liée au conflit depuis le début de l’année.

france24fr.title: L’Iran visé par de nouvelles sanctions économiques
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis renforcent leur offensive économique contre Téhéran avec un nouveau train de sanctions visant plus de 60 personnes, entreprises et navires liés aux revenus pétroliers, aux programmes balistique et nucléaire, ainsi qu’aux activités cybernétiques iraniennes. Washington entend priver le régime de ses ressources et accentuer son isolement international. Explications avec l'invité de France 24, Rémi Bourgeot, chercheur associé à l'Iris.

france24fr.title: Une nouvelle attaque de gangs fait au moins quarante morts en Haïti
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle attaque de gangs a semé la panique à Kenscoff, près de la capitale haïtienne. Dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, des hommes armés ont pris d’assaut cette commune située dans les hauteurs, faisant au moins quarante morts. Le point sur la situation avec Catherine Norris Trent, Grand Reporter France 24.

france24fr.title: Nouvelles sanctions américaines contre Téhéran et ses alliés
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis annoncent une nouvelle offensive économique contre l’Iran, destinée à "couper toutes les ressources" qui soutiennent le régime de Téhéran. Le Trésor américain sanctionne 60 personnes, entreprises et navires accusés de faciliter les revenus pétroliers iraniens, les achats d’armes ou les activités cybernétiques. Décryptage de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : la Française Sophie Adenot sort dans l'espace pour la deuxième fois
Afghanistan : un million d'enfants en danger de mort à cause de la malnutrition, selon l'Unicef
france24fr.description: Le Fonds des Nations unies pour l'enfance (Unicef) a prévenu mardi qu'un million d'enfants souffrant de malnutrition aiguë sévère se trouvent en danger de mort en Afghanistan si rien n'est fait pour leur venir en aide.

france24fr.title: Mali-Algérie : la visite de Maïga à Alger ouvre-t-elle la page de la réconciliation ?
france24fr.description: 🇲🇱 Après plusieurs années de tensions, le Mali et l’Algérie amorcent-ils un rapprochement ? En visite à Alger, le Premier ministre malien Abdoulaye Maïga a été reçu par son homologue algérien puis par le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune.

france24fr.title: "On a été bombardés par la nature" : l'état de choc à Pomas, village audois frappé par une tornade
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de la tornade qui a dévasté Pomas, village audois, ses administrés étaient encore, mardi, en "état de choc". Les dégâts témoignent de la violence de l'évènement : partout des gravats, des arbres arrachés, des tuiles, des véhicules éventrés ou renversés, des maisons aux vitres soufflées ou aux volets dégondés.

france24fr.title: Attentats du 11-Septembre : la généalogie génétique permet d'identifier une nouvelle victime
france24fr.description: La mairie de New York a annoncé lundi qu'une victime des attentats terroristes du 11-Septembre avait pu être identifiée pour la première fois grâce à la technique de la généalogie génétique médico-légale. Plus de 1 000 victimes de l'attentat le plus meurtrier commis sur le sol américain n'ont pas encore été identifiées.

france24fr.title: Ebola : la riposte s’organise sur le fleuve Congo
france24fr.description: Le virus Ebola touche désormais six provinces de la RDC. Face à sa propagation, le fleuve Congo devient un nouveau front de la riposte. Des milliers de passagers et de marchandises y circulent chaque jour, faisant du fleuve une potentielle voie de diffusion du virus.

france24fr.title: Trump menace de doubler les droits de douane sur les produits canadiens
france24fr.description: Après l’échec des négociations, le président américain menace de porter à 50% les droits de douane sur les voitures, les camions, les pièces automobiles et l’acier importés du Canada à compter du 1er janvier 2027, contre 25% aujourd’hui pour les véhicules. Le point sur la situation avec Joanne Profeta depuis Montréal.

france24fr.title: Six milliards d'euros saoudiens pour un mégaprojet de loisirs près de Paris
france24fr.description: La visite de Mohammed ben Salmane à Paris se traduit par une annonce d’investissement saoudien d’ampleur : 6 milliards d’euros seront consacrés à un complexe de trois parcs à thème à Cergy-Pontoise, près de Paris. Porté par le groupe saoudien Qiddiya, le projet doit créer jusqu’à 22 000 emplois directs et devenir l’un des plus grands investissements récents dans les loisirs en France. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: France : les images impressionnantes de la tornade à Pomas
france24fr.description: 🌪️ À Pomas, dans le sud de la France, une tornade a tout balayé sur son passage. Au moins 39 personnes sont blessées, et 300 habitations endommagées.

france24fr.title: À Chamonix, le succès de l'UTMB exaspère une partie des habitants
france24fr.description: L'Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc a débuté à Chamonix, avec son épreuve reine de 174 kilomètres autour du massif. Mais le succès grandissant de l'événement suscite aussi des critiques chez certains riverains, qui dénoncent ses effets sur la vie locale. Récit d'Alice Brogat et Carys Garland.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : le fleuve Congo, nouveau front face à la propagation d'Ebola
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l'épidémie d'Ebola s'étend désormais à six provinces. Les autorités redoutent une propagation du virus par le fleuve Congo, emprunté chaque jour par des milliers de passagers. Reportage d'Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

nzz.description: Bereits vor gut sieben Jahren hatte der Gerichtshof in Strassburg die Freilassung des türkischen Kulturförderers Kavala gefordert. Nun stellt das Gericht weitere Menschenrechtsverletzungen fest.

nzz.description: Ein Staatsanwalt, ein Starregisseur und neunzig Ziegen sind die Hauptdarsteller einer Sommergeschichte, die auf der Trauminsel im Golf von Neapel spielt.

nzz.description: Der VW-Chef Oliver Blume will den Konzern radikal umbauen, um ihn zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Belegschaft äussert bei den angelaufenen Betriebsversammlungen Kritik. Anfang September dürften erste Entscheide getroffen werden.

spiegel.description: Allein an den Händen hat North West mindestens zehn Piercings. Die würden sie vervollständigen, sagt die 13-Jährige. Zu einem Piercing sagen ihre Eltern Kim Kardashian und Kanye West jedoch Nein.

spiegel.description: Deutschland und die EU gehen auf die Taliban zu, um Abschiebungen nach Afghanistan leichter zu machen. Opfer des Regimes sind entsetzt.

spiegel.description: Lars Klingbeils Finanzministerium hat Eckpunkte für eine Zuckersteuer auf Getränke vorgelegt. Auch alkoholfreies Bier und Fruchtsäfte wären betroffen. Das Landwirtschaftsministerium hat nach SPIEGEL-Informationen Widerstand angekündigt.

spiegel.description: Nach einem Sprungversuch beim Diamond-League-Meeting in Kattowitz musste Malaika Mihambo ins Krankenhaus. Aber die Verletzung am Oberschenkel ist doch nicht so schwerwiegend, wie es zunächst aussah.

observador.description: 3,7 milhões de crianças estão em estado de subnutrição aguda. A UNICEF alerta que as mulheres grávidas também estão a ser afetadas, aumentando o número de bebés nascidos abaixo do peso.

observador.description: Guterres garante que as Nações Unidas não entraram em colapso e avisa para os riscos de um mundo multipolar, mais propenso a conflitos. Admite que o seu cargo não lhe confere poder, mas que tem "voz".

observador.description: O tenista português Gastão Elias, de 35 anos, anunciou o fim da sua carreira profissional. Elias despede-se após uma lesão no joelho e com a certeza de que deu "tudo o que tinha".

observador.description: O Presidente do Conselho Europeu pediu aos líderes da União Europeia responsabilidade coletiva, para chegar ao orçamento 2028-2034, até ao final do ano. Este acordo representa uma escolha política.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

phys-org.title: 'Now boarding' … 240,000 miles from Earth, at the moon's first airport
phys-org.description: The moon's getting its first airport, and it's about to get busy. Within the next two decades, NASA's planned Gateway—humanity's first lunar spaceport—may become a bustling hub for Orion crew capsules, lunar landers, cargo vehicles and astronauts traveling between Earth, the moon and, eventually, destinations in the deep unknown.

phys-org.title: Probing issues relevant to students boosts civic engagement
phys-org.description: When social studies students delve into issues that affect their communities and discuss them in class, they are more likely to consider other people's points of view and are generally more interested in voting and other ways of participating in civic life.

phys-org.title: Monitoring employee performance: The pitfalls for HR

phys-org.title: Cow gut enzyme could help target bacterial biofilms and antibiotic-resistant infections
phys-org.description: The bacterium Acinetobacter baumannii poses a substantial threat in health care settings, readily forming biofilms on wounds and medical surfaces and contributing to persistent infections and delayed healing. Its growing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and status as a WHO critical-priority pathogen underscore the urgent need for new wound management strategies. However, many current treatments are ineffective against its biofilms.

phys-org.title: Archaeologists investigate a feared young woman's 17th century vampiric grave in Poland

In what they call Grave 75, they uncovered the 400-year-old remains of a young adult woman buried in a very unusual and unsettling way. A curved iron sickle was placed directly over her neck, with its blade pointing toward her throat, while a triangular iron padlock was attached to the big toe of her left foot.

phys-org.title: Does heavy social media use damage your family's relationship?

phys-org.title: Large mammals alter soil chemistry and increase fertility in the Atlantic Forest
phys-org.description: A study published in the journal Ecological Monographs indicates that large mammals, such as tapirs, peccaries, agoutis and deer, alter the chemical composition of litter and soil in tropical forests of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. As a result, they increase nutrient availability and, possibly, soil fertility.

phys-org.title: The little red dots of our cosmos might hide something big

Reconstructing past diets at the level of individual food items is remarkably difficult. phys-org.title: AI helps workers most when paired with experience, new study finds
phys-org.description: As companies race to integrate artificial intelligence into the workplace, new research suggests workers benefit most when AI is paired with experience rather than treated as a replacement for it.

phys-org.title: Setting limits on phase transitions in the dark energy era
phys-org.description: The universe is known to be expanding at an accelerating rate. Physicists typically attribute this acceleration to dark energy, a mysterious component of the universe that exerts negative pressure, causing space to expand faster. Dark energy is thought to have become the predominant influence on the universe's evolution around 3–4 billion years ago, at the beginning of what is known as the dark energy era.

phys-org.title: Study finds sustainable farming program helps refugees, immigrants boost health while launching agribusinesses
phys-org.description: The slang term "touch grass" encourages people to step away from the internet or devices and connect with the real world. New research from the University of Kansas has found that a project that helps resettled refugees and immigrants learn sustainable farming has many of the term's same benefits, improving people's mental and physical well-being and training them to run independent agricultural businesses.

phys-org.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
phys-org.description: Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.

phys-org.title: The hidden chemistry behind glow-in-the-dark art
phys-org.description: Some of the world's brightest colors don't just reflect light; they create it. Scientists and museum conservators are now uncovering why these luminous pigments fade and how to preserve them for future generations. The findings could help protect artwork while informing the development of longer-lasting phosphorescent materials for a variety of applications, from fashion runways to airport runways.

phys-org.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
phys-org.description: Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry.

phys-org.title: Tides can vary by almost a meter across a single bay, four decades of satellite images reveal
phys-org.description: Tide levels can vary by almost a meter across a single bay, according to a new study that uses decades of satellite images to measure tides at the scale of individual beaches.

phys-org.title: Bright ideas accelerate the hunt for quantum emitters
phys-org.description: The search for materials that can power future quantum technologies is accelerating, but identifying the most promising candidates remains painfully slow. Evaluating whether a material can efficiently emit quantum light requires computationally intensive simulations, making it difficult to screen the vast number of available materials.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: China’s Platform State and the AI Race
proj-syn.description: Balancing regulation with innovation is never easy, and the Chinese government’s robust support for AI could lead to inefficiency and excess. But the “platform state” model, combined with other strengths, has enabled China to achieve dominance in multiple strategic sectors, while enhancing its resilience.

proj-syn.title: Which Future for Online Life?
proj-syn.description: By articulating a vision of the future that seems inevitable, technology industry leaders want to create the impression that the surrender of privacy and other defining trends of the current moment cannot be stopped. But predictions become self-fulfilling prophecies only if we believe them and act accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Pro-Human Vision
proj-syn.description: The original vision of the internet as a democratizing force failed to account for the manner in which power would concentrate, attention would be monetized, and public discourse would be manipulated. In Europe and elsewhere, these lessons now must inform how we govern generative AI.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: Will We Preserve the Sources of Human Learning?
proj-syn.description: By obscuring or destroying the primary sources of knowledge, large language models create the illusion of an embodied and active collection of everything we know. But without examining and interrogating the human originators of recorded knowledge and wisdom, one cannot fully develop one’s own understanding.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.
